abstract: A Barnette graph is simple, cubic, $3$-connected, bipartite and planar. It has the global $H^{+-}$ property if, for every ordered pair of distinct edges $(e,f)$, some Hamilton cycle contains $e$ and avoids $f$. Barnette's conjecture has been proved (OpenAI, 2026; exposition by Z. Li, arXiv:2610.30490), and with it $P_2$-, $P_4$-Hamiltonicity, $H^-$ and the $H^{+-}$ condition for edge pairs at distance at most $1$ hold for every Barnette graph; global $H^{+-}$ for all Barnette graphs remains open. All Barnette graphs on at most $66$ vertices are known computationally to have it, and infinite families follow from tight-cut composition. We give a controlled expansion mechanism with an explicit growth rate. Starting from the cube, we iterate legal $C_4$-expansions at two recurrent sites. An exact six-traversal criterion describes the Hamilton cycles of one expansion in terms of parent structures. A finite signed-support invariant (22 states, or 40 when reflected orientations are allowed), initialised by explicit cube witnesses, then shows that every construction word yields a Barnette graph with global $H^{+-}$. A rooted grammar argument shows that depth $k$ produces exactly $2^{\max(k-2,0)}$ boundary-pointwise isomorphism types. A cubic embedding bound turns this into $B_{H^{+-}}(8+4k)\ge\lceil 2^{\max(k-2,0)}/((8+4k)3^{7})\rceil$, so $B_{H^{+-}}(n)\ge 2^{n/4-O(\log n)}$ along $n\equiv 0 \pmod 4$. Exhaustive computer checks agree with these statements for all standard words with $n\le 32$ and all reflected words with $n\le 28$. Limitations: the result concerns two specific expansion sites, not arbitrary $C_4$-expansions. The explicit bound first exceeds $1$ at $n=88$. A 2005 edge-replacement scheme of Kao and Chen could not be consulted in full, so we make no absolute priority claim. The work was developed with AI assistance and has not been independently reviewed by experts.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Cites the proof of Barnette's conjecture by OpenAI (openai/math Family 180, preprint dated 24 September 2026, released 6 October 2026) and Z. Li's exposition (arXiv:2610.30490).
2. Introduction and abstract now state that $P_2$, $P_4$, $H^-$ and the $H^{+-}$ condition for edge pairs at distance at most $1$ hold for all Barnette graphs, with a two-line derivation from $P_4$; the contribution is positioned as explicit recursive families with global $H^{+-}$ and their exponential count, global $H^{+-}$ for all Barnette graphs being open.
3. Removed statements made obsolete by this ("nothing is claimed about Barnette's conjecture", the novelty caveat on recursive $P_2$-Hamiltonian families). The Kao–Chen 2005 caveat is retained. No mathematical change.
title: Exponentially Many Barnette Graphs with the Global $H^{+-}$ Property
